channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: A $7 Billion Gas Bill Sees Developing Asian Nations Sour on LNG
item.description: The loss of a fifth of liquefied natural gas supply due to the US-Iran war is blowing out costs for Asia’s developing markets, and forcing a rethink of the fuel’s long-term future in the region.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Stapczynski and Sing Yee Ong

item.title: Trump’s Drug-Pricing Push to Cut Access Outside US, Study Finds
item.description: The Trump administration’s push to bring US drug spending down is a powerful incentive for pharmaceutical companies to boost prices and reduce access elsewhere in the world, a study found.
item.dc:creator: Naomi Kresge

item.title: US Stock Futures Fall on AI Jitters, Oil Gains: Markets Wrap
item.description: US equity-index futures retreated after major artificial intelligence companies called for a slowdown in the technology’s development, raising concerns about a sector that has powered this year’s stock rally. Oil advanced.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Burgess and Anand Krishnamoorthy

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Sept. 14
item.description: Oil advanced after Saudi Arabia shut a major crude pipeline following attacks, disrupting a route that’s been used to bypass the Strait of Hormuz during the US-Iran war and deepening a global energy crunch.
item.dc:creator: Kanoko Matsuyama

item.title: Hormuz Meeting With Iran and Gulf Nations Delayed, Oman Says
item.description: A planned meeting for Monday between Iran and several Gulf nations on creating a temporary shipping lane through the Strait of Hormuz has been postponed, according to Oman’s foreign minister.
item.dc:creator: Sherif Tarek

item.title: A 5% Treasury Yield Is Raising New Risks for Markets, Economy
item.description: The bond selloff has driven a key Treasury yield to the verge of 5%, worsening angst from Wall Street to Washington about the higher borrowing costs hitting the US economy.
item.dc:creator: Greg Ritchie and Michael MacKenzie

item.title: Bloomberg This Weekend 09/13/2026
item.description: The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo bring clarity, context and a bit of humor to the weekend’s biggest headlines, LIVE from New York. Joined by Journalist & Features Writer Isabel Woodford, BMO Capital Markets Senior Economist Jennifer Lee, Delaware Sen. Chris Coons and GasBuddy Head of Petroleum Analysis Patrick De Haan. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Noel Tata Faces Biggest Crisis Yet With Regulator’s IPO Order
item.description: The Indian banking regulator’s refusal to exempt Tata Sons Pvt. from a public listing-rule comes as an unexpected blow for group patriarch Noel Tata, who’s already struggling to address leadership uncertainty at the top of the $185 billion conglomerate.
item.dc:creator: Saikat Das, Anto Antony, P R Sanjai and Satviki Sanjay

item.title: By The Way: Headlines You May Have Missed
item.description: The middle-class side-hustle, mean girl moms, and the 2026 Emmy awards: Watch Lisa Mateo, Christina Ruffini and Jeff Mason talk about headlines from this week you may have missed on Bloomberg This Weekend! (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Refining Bottleneck Sends Diesel to Record High
item.description: Record diesel prices are exposing a critical constraint in global energy markets as refinery disruptions abroad collide with limited capacity in the US. GasBuddy’s Patrick De Haan is on Bloomberg This Weekend and says producing more crude alone won’t solve the problem because refiners are already operating near their limits, leaving little room to boost gasoline and diesel supplies quickly. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Drone Threats Force Cities to Rethink Defenses
item.description: As drones become cheaper, faster and harder to detect, cities far from traditional battlefields are confronting the challenge of protecting civilians without creating new risks from falling debris or costly interceptions. Bloomberg Weekend Senior Writer Morgan Meaker is on Bloomberg This Weekend and examines how governments are testing everything from jammers and interceptor drones to surprisingly effective low tech nets as they search for defenses that can keep pace with rapidly evolving threats. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Shelton Eyes End to US Men’s Grand Slam Drought
item.description: Ben Shelton heads into the US Open final with a chance to become the first American man to win a Grand Slam singles title since Andy Roddick in 2003, potentially giving US men’s tennis a new marquee star. Bloomberg News Business of Sports Reporter Vanessa Perdomo joins David Gura and Christina Ruffini on Bloomberg This Weekend to discuss Shelton and also broader questions across sports ranging from college eligibility rules to the NFL’s push into international markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Will Silicon Valley Rearm America?
item.description: War in Ukraine, conflict in the Middle East and the rise of China have pushed national security back to the center of US economic and industrial strategy. Former Defense Secretary Mark Esper says the country needs to spend more on defense and better use cutting-edge weapons coming out of places like Silicon Valley, Austin and Boston. The opportunity is particularly striking in space, where companies like Apex Space are trying to industrialize satellite production as the US considers ambitious projects like Golden Dome . But the new defense-tech boom still faces hard questions: will the Pentagon procure quickly enough; will startups scale production; is space-based missile defense technically and financially realistic; and will the future belong to startups, legacy primes, or a marriage between the two? (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: LIV Golf’s $5 Billion Path to Bankruptcy
item.description: LIV shook professional golf with flashy tournaments and big payouts, thanks to billions of dollars in backing from the Saudi sovereign wealth fund. On today’s Big Take podcast, David Gura and Golf.com senior writer Sean Zak look at why LIV Golf couldn’t make the cut — and how it changed pro golf. Listen wherever you get your podcasts. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Traders Hedging Stock Rally Split on Plunge or Drift Protection
item.description: Investors looking to hedge as the equity rally stalls in the face of rising interest rates and oil prices are split between protecting against a fast selloff or a slow grind lower.
item.dc:creator: Christian Dass

item.title: Trump Urges Zelenskyy to Stop Hitting Russia’s Diesel Refineries
item.description: President Donald Trump says Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has to stop striking Russia’s diesel fuel refineries because it’s “hurting the world.”
item.dc:creator: Sam Kim

item.title: Wall Street Says Stay With Stocks Despite Late ‘90s Dot-Com Vibe
item.description: Rising bond yields and soaring oil prices have many Wall Street pros looking back a few decades to the volatile period before the dot-com crash. But that doesn’t mean they’re encouraging investors to dump their stocks.
item.dc:creator: Geoffrey Morgan

item.title: After Oil Surge and War, Emerging Markets Unfazed by Fed Risk
item.description: Emerging markets have defied war, $100 oil and rising Treasury yields this year. And despite worries of a US interest-rate hike, investors see reasons for this year’s rally to keep going.
item.dc:creator: Selcuk Gokoluk and Peter Laca

item.title: Iran Seeks Gulf Support for Hormuz Plan
item.description: Gulf states are weighing how to respond to Iran’s push for a new arrangement governing the Strait of Hormuz as continued attacks threaten shipping and drive up energy costs. On Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg News Middle East Reporter Dan Williams and Bloomberg News White House Correspondent Skylar Woodhouse discuss growing regional frustration with the conflict, pressure on US allies and signs Gulf governments may be looking for a larger role in shaping a path forward. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ukraine Says Passenger Train Headed to Warsaw Hit by Drone
item.description: The locomotive of a passenger train traveling from Kyiv to Warsaw was hit by a Russian drone just kilometers from the Polish border on Sunday morning, Ukraine’s foreign minister said, as Moscow’s airstrikes push closer to NATO territory.
item.dc:creator: Ros Krasny
